subject: Hosted vs Dedicated decision follow-up: latency & throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@finpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the time earlier today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. Great call, Evan/Priya. Key points I captured from the session: 

- Primary goal: integrate LLM chat into main product for interactive support (chat+actions).
- Latency target: p95 ideally < 150ms for short responses (~30–60 tokens).
- Throughput: expected peak ~1,000 req/s (concurrent ~800 users), sustained working hours traffic shape with spikes ~1,200 req/s.
- Functional: deterministic behavior, prefix caching for repeated prompts, and availability during peak hours.
- Compliance: standard enterprise requirements, but data residency is US-only for now (no air-gapped).

Based on the call, the two realistic hosting options are:

1) Hosted API (Redwood managed): fastest to get started. Pros: minimal ops, automatic routing, transparent performance dashboards. Cons: at very high, sustained peaks p95 can vary depending on shared capacity and colocation; we offer burst/bandwidth options but not the same predictability as dedicated.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): provides predictable throughput and tighter latency SLOs — we can reserve node pools dedicated to FinPay, configure autoscale/burst policies, and run pre-production perf tests on the exact prompt mix. Recommended if you need guaranteed p95 at 150ms or lower under sustained 1k+ req/s.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a short comparison doc and an MA timeline draft (attached).
- If you confirm the numbers above are accurate, we’ll schedule a 60-min technical workshop (solutions + infra) to:
  a) run a short perf benchmark on representative prompts
  b) propose node sizing and autoscale policy
  c) give a 30-day pilot quote for Dedicated capacity (if you want predictability)

Can you confirm the p95 target (150ms) and peak estimate (~1k req/s)? Also let us know any additional constraints (e.g., stricter data residency, on-prem requirement) so we can include Private/VPC as an option if needed.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa in for sizing notes.

—
Neha Kapoor

neha@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0126

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Evan. Short answer up front: for a hard p95 <150ms at sustained 1k req/s we should plan for Dedicated capacity. Hosted can occasionally meet that at lower sustained loads and with regional routing + aggressive cache/batching tuning, but it won’t give the same deterministic guarantees under continuous peak.

Here’s a bit more detail to help you decide: 

- Hosted API:
  - Typical p95 for short generations (30–60 tokens) on shared hosted nodes in a single region: ~120–220ms depending on load and model (we’ve seen as low as 110ms for optimized prompts at low load).
  - At sustained 1k+ req/s, p95 variance increases; we recommend Hosted for teams that prioritize time-to-market and cost elasticity over strict latency SLOs.

- Dedicated capacity (recommended):
  - We reserve a private GPU pool for FinPay; with a 4x A10G baseline and autoscale to 8x during peaks, we expect p95 ~110–140ms for 40-token responses on our benchmark prompts (we’ll verify with your prompts).
  - Predictable throughput: capacity planning and canary rollouts let you keep p95 stable during spikes.
  - Additional: reserved KV cache warm-up for repeated prompts reduces effective token compute.

Quick cost guidance (very rough):
- Hosted (managed, pay-as-you-go + burst): lower startup cost, variable monthly depending on tokens/requests.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): commit to monthly spend for the pool; higher baseline, but better unit economics at scale and more predictable. I’ll have Marissa share a precise estimate post-workshop; provisional pilot pricing will be included in that package.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Tech workshop: 60 minutes (solutions + infra). Please share a 20–30 prompt sample set (representative of chat average length) and a target SLA matrix.
2) Redwood runs perf benchmark against your prompt set in both Hosted and Dedicated staging configs and returns p95 numbers + config recommendation.
3) If Dedicated is preferred, we can scope a 30-day pilot with a minimal reserved commit and detailed procurement steps.

I’ve attached a short benchmark instructions file that explains sampling and data redaction steps. If Thurs next week is good for timing, we’ll schedule and include Marissa for sizing and Dylan for infra detail.

Cheers —
Neha

Attachments: benchmark-instructions.txt

Looping in a brief SRE/solutions note and a proposed starter configuration. Quoting Neha’s summary below for context.

Quoted: 
> - p95 target: 150ms
> - Peak: ~1,000 req/s

Sizing notes (starter):
- Baseline: 4x A10G nodes (single shard) with reserved pool for FinPay; autoscale policy to 8x for sustained bursts.
- Expected performance (internal estimate, will validate with your prompts): p95 ~120ms for 40-token responses; p50 ~35–45ms.
- Autoscale settings: scale-up threshold = 70% GPU util; scale-down cooldown = 10m; warm pool for prefix/KV cache.

Procurement / pilot steps:
1) Sign pilot MSA addendum + minimum 30-day reserved commit (we’ll send a one-page SOW).
2) Redwood provisions the dedicated pool in your preferred US region and runs the benchmark (you provide 20–30 prompts).
3) Post-benchmark we recommend either: a) continue on Dedicated with a 3–6 month commit for better unit cost or b) revert to Hosted with configured burst policy and cache tuning.

Preliminary cost band (very rough): 4x A10G reserved baseline + autoscale to 8x = ballpark $48k–$65k/mo depending on reserved term and support level. We’ll refine after the workshop.

If everyone’s aligned I’ll send a 60-min invite for Thurs next week (we have a slot 2026-03-11 11:00am PT).
